 JUDGMENT

The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road accident dated 23.03.2019.
2.

The case of the Petitioner in brief is that, on 23.03.2019 at about 08.30 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding in motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA02HN3565 as a pillion rider alongwith his friend Venu who was riding the said motorcycle near Chikkatorepalya Bridge, Magadi road, in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life and due to avoid the opposite vehicle suddenly took his motorcycle on the edge of the road and lost control and skid from the said motorcycle and due to impact he sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was taken to Kenganar Hospital, Magadi road wherein admitted as an inpatient and underwent surgery and discharged with an advise.

So far his parents have spent Rs.3,75,000/ towards treatment and Rs.25,000/ towards conveyance and nourishment etc., and he has to incur future medical expenses also.
3.
The petitioner further averred that, at the time of accident he was hale and healthy and was an Auto driver and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/ p.m..
Due to the accidental injuries he could not attend his work and he is not able to lead his normal life due to his permanent physical disability.
The Tavarekere Police have registered a criminal case against the rider of the motorcycle in Cr.No.101/2019 for the offences punishable u/Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.
Hence, the 1 st respondent being the owner and the 2nd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to him.
4. In response to service of notice issued by this court/Tribunal, the Respondent No.2 has appeared and filed written statement.
In spite of due service of summons, the Respondent No.1 did not appear and hence placed exparte.

5. The Respondent No.2 in the written statement have denied the case of the petitioner as false,
admitted the issuance of policy but their liability is subject to its terms and conditions and submitted that there is non compliance of Section 134(c) and Section 158(6) of M.V. Act.

Further Sri.Naveen Kumar M vs Sri.H.G.Srinivas Gowda on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14108808/
2 submitted that there was no rash and negligence on the part of the rider of motorcycle as he was proceeding slowly and cautiously on the left side of the road near Chikkatorepalya Bridge, Magadi Road, at that time a vehicle suddenly came from opposite side in a wrong side in rash and negligent manner endangering human life and the rider of the bike turned it on the safer side in order to avoid the opposite vehicle hitting his bike and in the process the rider of the motorcycle skid resulting in some minor injuries to the pillion rider.

sentences.text: They have issued policy to the bike is two wheelers liability only policy.

As per the General Exclusion No.4 of the MOTORISED TWO WHEELERS LIABILITY ONLY POLICY, it is not liable in respect death or bodily injury to any person carried in on the motorcycle and as the petitioner was travelling in the vehicle as a pillion rider, hence they are not liable to pay any compensation under the policy.
Further submitted that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective DL to drive the same and hence there is breach of policy conditions.
Therefore, dismissal of the petition against them.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings, the issues are framed as under:

Whether the Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 23.03.2019 at about 08.30 p.m., near Chikkathorepalya Bridge, Magadi Bengaluru Road, Kasaba Hobli, Magadi Taluk,
Ramanagar, due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA 02HN 3565 by its rider as alleged?
2. Whether the Petitioner proves that he is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.
What order or award?

Dr.Chunchesh M.D. Consultant Orthopaedic Surgeon at Kenganar Hospital, is examined as PW.2 and produced documents as per Exs.P12 to P16.

On the other side the Respondent No.2 have examined its Deputy Manager as RW.1 and got marked documents as per Exs.R.1 to R3.
8.
Heard the arguments and perused the materials on record.
The counsel for the respondent No.2 has filed written arguments.

The counsel for the petitioner has relied upon decision rendered by Hon'ble High Court of Punjab and Haryana in Shiv Lochan Singh @ Bhola Vs. National Ins.Co. &
others dated 27.11.2017.

3 10. Issue No.1: The Petitioner in order to prove that the accident was occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA02HN3565 has examined himself as PW.1 and produced 6 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.5 and P7.

He has specifically stated in his evidence that, on 23.03.2019 at about 08.30 p.m., he was proceeding in motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA02HN3565 as a pillion rider alongwith his friend Venu riding the said motorcycle near Chikkatorepalya Bridge, Magadi road, in a rash and negligent manner,
endangering to human life, when an another vehicle came from opposite side the rider of two wheeler suddenly took his vehicle on the edge of the road, impact of the same both fell down by losing control over the bike and caused the accident.

The Respondent No.2 insurer has denied that the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle and contended that they are not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner under the policy as it is only a liability only policy.

In the crossexamination of PW.1 it is brought out that as one car was coming from their front side and hence the rider took the bike towards left side or otherwise the car could have caused accident, due to time sense of the rider of the bike his life is saved, on that day the rider of the bike was riding the bike slowly and cautiously.

11. The respondent No.2 in support of their defence have got examined their official as RW.1 who has reiterated the averments of their written statement in his examination in chief and his evidence is more focused that they are not liable to pay compensation under the policy.
He has produced the true copy of the policy schedule, notice to insured with returned postal cover and authorization letter.

In the crossexamination of RW.1 it is elicited that they have issued liability only policy to the insured subject to its terms and conditions, as per them the pillion rider is treated as gratuitous passenger.

The counsel for the petitioner has crossexamined the RW.1 at length with regard to comprehensive policy and liability only policy and about IRDI rules but nothing worth is elicited to accept the claim of the petitioner that the pillion rider comes under the definition of third party and he is covered under the Liability only policy.

12. No doubt the PW.1 admitted that the rider of the bike in order to avoid accident was being caused by the car which was coming from their front side got turned the bike towards left side and he was riding his bike slowly and cautiously, this itself does not amount that the rider of the bike was not rash or negligent in riding the bike because being a user of vehicle in road it is his duty to foresee the oncoming vehicles and judge correctly to go safely in the road but from the act of the rider of the bike it appears that there was clearly misjudgment by the rider and to avoid the car got turned the bike and hence it is clear case of negligence on the part of the rider of the bike.
Moreover the case is registered against the rider of the bike only.

The respondent No.2 has not lead any evidence to prove their defence that the rider of the bike was not negligent but on materials on record clearly shows that the rider did misjudgment which lead to accident no matter whether it was to avoid a major collision between the car and the bike 13.

Further, the Petitioner apart from his oral evidence has produced the documents such as FIR,
FIS, spot mahazar, seizure Mahazar, MVA report and charge sheet as per Exs.P.1 to P.5 and P7 and they are public documents which have got presumptive value under law and in absence of contrary evidence the said documents needs to be appreciated in favour of petitioner.

The Ex.P.7 which is the copy of charge sheet filed in Cr.No.101/2019 clearly discloses that the investigation officer has filed Sri.Naveen Kumar M vs Sri.H.G.Srinivas Gowda on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14108808/

As such, there are no reasons to disbelieve the version of the Petitioner and accept the version of the Respondent No.2.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.5 and P7, this court is of the opinion that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA02HN3565 and same has resulted in grievous injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.

14. Issue No.2: The Petitioner has further averred that, on account of accident, he is not able to lead his normal life due to permanent physical disability and hence he is unable to do his earlier work/occupation.
The Petitioner in this regard has entered into witness box and deposed that due to the accidental injuries, he is suffering from permanent disability.
Apart from that, he has produced the wound certificate as per Ex.P.6.
As per Ex.P.6, the Petitioner has sustained fracture left femur and compound fracture both bones left tibia and fibula, and the doctor opined that injuries are grievous in nature.

The Ex.P8/discharge summary issued by Kenganar Hospital wherein treated as an inpatient from 23.03.2019 to 05.04.2019 and underwent surgery for left femur IMIL with nailing done and for left tibia IMIL with nailing done and for left fibula dual plating done on 24.03.2019 and discharged with advise for follow up treatment.
The petitioner has got examined Dr.Chunchesh M.D. as PW.2.
This court while considering the Issue No.1 has already come to the conclusion that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation from the Respondents.
Disability 15.

In the chiefexamination, the PW.2 has deposed that, on 23.03.2019 patient by name Mr.Naveen Kumar M., aged about 20 years, had come to their hospital with an history of RTA and admitted as an inpatient from 23.03.2019 to 05.04.2019, during the said period he was treated him personally,
did sustain closed left shaft of femur fracture and closed left shaft of tibia and fibula fracture and underwent surgery for left femur CRIF with IMIL and locking bolt, left tibiaCRIF with IMIL and locking bolt, left fibulaORIF with dual plating, Postoperative period was uneventful and discharged on 05.04.2019 with an advise of regular dressing, physiotheraphy and regular follow up.

On appreciating the evidence on record, the treatment taken by the petitioner and the injuries sustained by the petitioner, the whole body functional disability of petitioner is considered as 12% only.
Monthly income 16.
The Petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, he was an Auto driver and earning sum of Rs.20,000/ p.m..
But, to substantiate this, the Petitioner has not examined any witness or produced any documents in this regard.
Therefore, the version of the Petitioner that he was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/ per month is not acceptable.
At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged about 20 years as could be make out from Ex.P.11/copy of Adhaar card of the petitioner.
The accident took place in the year 2019.

Therefore, having regard to the age of the petitioner and also relying the decision of Hon'ble H.C. in the case of Sumangala & Others and Ramanagouda & Anr., in MFA No:202534/2019(MVC) wherein the notified notional income chart of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is considered for fixing the notional income and accordingly the monthly notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.14,000/ per month.

As such, Petitioner is entitled for the following compensation:
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:

After the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to Kenganar Hospital,
treated as an inpatient from 23.03.2019 to 05.04.2019 wherein left femur IMIL with nailing done and for left tibia IMIL with nailing done and for left fibula dual plating done on 24.03.2019 and discharged with advise for follow up treatment.
Considering the nature of injuries and duration of treatment he has underwent, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.50,000/ under this head.
ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent more than a sum of Rs.3,75,000/ towards treatment.

under the head of Medical Expenses.
iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and underwent treatment.
After the accident, the Petitioner was taken treatment in the above mentioned hospital.
Therefore, considering the nature of injuries and the duration of treatment it can be said that the Petitioner has required at least two months time for recovering from the injuries sustained by him.

Hence, he is entitled for a sum of Rs.28,000/ under Sri.Naveen Kumar M vs Sri.H.G.Srinivas Gowda on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14108808/

sentences.text: iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:
In so far as age of the Petitioner is concerned, the Petitioner has produced Aadhaar card as per Ex.P.11.
As per this document his age was 20 years as on the date of accident.
The Respondents have not placed any contrary document.
Therefore, as on the date of the accident the Petitioner's age is considered as 20 years.

(v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND  HAPPINESS:
The Petitioner was aged about 20 years at the time of accident.
He has sustained grievous injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 12% permanent disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life.
Because of this he will have to loose some amenities and comforts.
Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered a sum of Rs.20,000/ is awarded under this head.

vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND  NOURISHMENT CHARGES:
After the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to Kenganar Hospital, treated as an inpatient from 23.03.2019 to 05.04.2019 for 14 days.
He has spent Rs.25,000/ towards conveyance and nourishment etc..
In this regard he has not produced any documents.
Therefore, as during this period he must have spent considerable amount on his conveyance, attendant charges, food and nourishment etc..
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/ under this head.
vii) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
As per the version of the PW.2, the Petitioner requires second surgery for implant removal and it will cost approximately Rs.60,000/.
But there is no estimation bill produced by the Petitioner or PW.2.

Therefore, looking to the earlier treatment cost and nature of injuries and cross examination of PW.2, it appears it would be justifiable if an amount of Rs.25,000/ is awarded to the Petitioner under this head.
Therefore the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.25,000/ under this head.

LIABILITY :
18.

The Respondent No.2 contended that they have issued Liability only policy under which the petitioner being pillion rider is not covered and hence they are not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.

As discussed above the respondent No.2 has lead evidence of RW.1 and the counsel for the petitioner has crossexamined the RW.1 but nothing worth is elicited to accept the claim of the petitioner that the petitioner being pillion rider comes under third party and is covered under the policy issued to the insured vehicle.
19.

The petitioner in support of his claim that the petitioner being pillion rider is a third party and covered under the Liability only policy has placed reliance on the decision referred but it is not applicable in view of decision of our Hon'ble H.C. in AIR Online 2020 Kar 2610 :

Divisional Manager, United India Ins. Co., Ltd., Gulbarga Vs. Shamaraya Basanna Kattimani (MFA No.31781/2010), wherein the Hon'ble HC in the case of DM, United India Ins.
Co. Ltd. Vs. Shamaraya Basanna Kattimani has observed at Para 20, 22, 25, 26, 27,
31, 32, 33, 34 as held under:
20.

Therefore, from the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the above referred judgments,
the ratio laid down by this Court except Sri Purushotham T.M's case (supra) and by the Madras High Court (supra) it is settled principle of law that under the 'Act Policy/Statutory Policy/liability only policy', the occupants of the car/jeep or pillion rider on motorcycle the risk is not covered as they are not to be categorized as third parties.

But under the 'Comprehensive Policy/Package Policy/
liability only policy', the risk of occupants of the car/jeep or pillion on motorcycle are covered as the insured(owner) has entered into contract of insurance with the Insurer for covering risk at higher degree by making payment of extra premium above the horizon of covering risk under the 'Statutory Policy'.

Therefore, it is dictum in the above cited judgments if extra premium is not paid covering the risk of the occupants of the car/jeep or pillion on motorcycle, the Insurance Companies are not liable to indemnify the owner by making payment of compensation.
22. Chapter X of the M.V.Act stipulates regarding liability on the Insurance Companies 'without fault' in certain cases.
Therefore, Chapter X of the M.V.Act is dealing with liability of payment of compensation on the principle "no fault liability'.

Chapter XI of the M.V.Act deals with insurance of Sri.Naveen Kumar M vs Sri.H.G.Srinivas Gowda on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14108808/
8 motor vehicles against third party risks.

sentences.text: The provisions in Chapter XI and XII of the M.V.Act deals with procedures regarding award of compensation, liability on the owner and insurance companies etc.
Section 145 of the M.V.Act gives the definitions.

Clause (g) only stipulates the "third party"
includes the Government (before amendment Act 2019).
Section 146 of the M.VAct deals with necessity for insurance against third party risk.
Section 147 of the M.V.Act stipulates regarding requirements of policies and limits of liability.
Therefore, there are no definitions in the M.V.Act defining the term 'Act Policy/Statutory Policy/liability only policy' and 'Comprehensive Policy/Package Policy'.
These terminology are evolved and generated through the wordings used in the M.V.Act.
Therefore, these terminologies are used which arose out of practice of purchase of insurance policies keeping in view the degree of covering risk.
Covering risk of third party is mandatorly made by the statute.
Unless a vehicle is made insured compulsorily so far as covering risk of third party, that vehicle shall not be used on the public places or even in private premises for plying.
Therefore every insured shall purchase insurance policy compulsorily covering risk of third parties before making use the said vehicle for plying either in public place or in private place.
Therefore, the terminology of 'Act Policy/Statutory Policy/liability only policy' is being used.

Therefore, the contract of insurance between the insured and insurer in case of covering risk of third parties is compulsorily made and for this the owner of the vehicle has to pay a minimum amount of premium compulsorily as this type of insurance policy is called as 'Act policy/Statutory Policy/liability only policy'.

Whereas, if the owner intends to cover higher degree of risk above the covering risk of third parties so as to include covering risk of occupants in the car/jeep or pillion rider on the motorcycle or damaged caused to the vehicle the owner has to pay higher amount of premium covering the risk comprehensively.
Therefore, above the degree of covering the risk of third parties, if the owner intends to cover risk on higher degree as above stated it is because of on own volition of insurer and insured.
Therefore, the degree of covering risk of covering third party only or covering higher degree of risk that depends upon payment of extra premium.
Therefore if extra premium is paid on the own volition of the insured (owner) then it covers higher degree of risk, otherwise not.
25. Therefore, there is clear distinction is made between the passengers carrying in 'private service vehicle' and 'public service vehicle'.
Insured (owner) is first party and insurer is second party.

Therefore, the persons who are outside the offending vehicle or may be passengers in another vehicle if it meets with accident by offending vehicle are only terms as third parties considering the definitions enshrined in Section 2(33)
of and Section 2(35) of the M.V.Act with reference to the types of passengers in the said nature of vehicles.
Section 147 of the M.V.Act does not require a policy to cover the risk to passengers who are not carried for hire or reward.

The statutory insurance as mandated in Section 147 of the M.V.Act does not cover injuries suffered by the occupants of the private vehicle or death of the occupants is caused in the accident whether they are carried for hire or reward or not then they are not to be categorized Sri.Naveen Kumar M vs Sri.H.G.Srinivas Gowda on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14108808/
9 as third parties and as such the insurer cannot be held liable under Section 147 of the M.V.Act.

sentences.text:
Therefore, considering the definitions enshrined in Section 2(33) and Section 2(35) and Section 147 of the M.V.Act and if they are read harmoniously, the occupants/passengers/inmates of a private vehicle do not fall within the definition of category as third parties. Therefore, the legal obligations made as per Section 147 of the M.V.Act is only to the third parties stated above to those persons stated therein and it cannot extend to the occupants of the car/jeep or pillion rider on the motorcycle as they are not carried for hire or reward in a private service vehicle,
hence, they are not third parties.
26. In public service vehicle the carriage of passengers is on hire or reward basis and for that terms of contract of insurance is different.
But, in private service vehicle the passengers are not carried for hire or reward basis, simply they are occupants in the private service vehicle.
Even giving private service vehicle on hire or reward basis is not correct as per law.
Therefore, the terms of contract of insurance in so far as private service vehicle is concerned is different.

For private service vehicle, it is compulsory to purchase insurance policy for third parties are concerned, but is an option so far as covering risk of occupants in the private service vehicle is concerned.
Therefore, in private service vehicle for covering risk of occupants an additional premium is to be paid.

Hence, in these context, the Hon'ble Apex Court were pleased to make difference between the nature of 'Act Policy/Statutory Policy/Liability only policy" on one hand and 'Comprehensive Policy' on other hand in the judgment stated supra.

Therefore, Section 147 of the M.V.Act only covers the risk of third party and to cover the risk in respect of the persons stated therein, but, certainly does not extend covering risk of occupants of the car/jeep or pillion rider on the motorcycle.

27. As discussed above, if insured (owner) intends to cover higher degree of risk than what is covering risk of third parties, then, the insured (owner) shall pay additional premium and it is on volition of insurer and insured as it is pure contract between them in this regard.
In absence of payment of additional premium covering risk of the persons at higher degree apart from third parties, then the insurance companies are not liable to pay compensation.
Therefore, under Section 147 of the M.V.Act the liability arising out of statutory requirement stated therein.
31. Therefore, the ratio laid down in the Meena Variyal's case (supra) is squarely applicable to the present facts, circumstances involved in these cases.

Section 147 of the M.V.Act prescribes, requirements of policy of insurance and limits of liability,
while in the proviso appended thereto carves out an exception to the main provision.
It prescribes compulsorily coverage of risk to third parties and to those who are stated in the said provision.

Therefore, unless the purchase of insurance policy compulsorily at minimal covering the risk of third parties, the owner cannot ply the vehicles on road or on public places and also in private places.
Therefore, the provisions of the M.V.Act are benevolent in nature protecting right and interest of victims arising out of accident particularly who are third parties.

sentences.text: Therefore, for covering risk for occupant in the car/jeep or pillion rider on the motorcycle, then the owner has to pay additional premium.
Therefore, proof of additional premium is a pure question of fact.

Therefore, where compulsorily purchase of insurance policy covering third parties only the insurance policy is 'Act'
Policy/Statutory Policy/liability only policy' but under this 'Act Policy/Statutory Policy/ liability only policy' the risk of occupant of the car/jeep or pillion rider is not covered as they are not be categorized as third parties.

Therefore, by this judgment it is held that under the 'Act Policy/Statutory Policy/ liability only policy', the risk of occupant of the jeep/car or pillion rider is not covered hence the Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation in respect of death or bodily injury occurred to the occupant of the car/jeep or pillion rider.

Therefore, under these circumstances the appeal filed by the Insurance Companies in the cases of putting burden on the Insurance Companies to pay compensation, are hereby allowed as putting burden on the Insurance Companies are erroneous, thus putting burden on Insurance Companies is set-aside.
Consequently, the appeal filed by the claimants and owners of the vehicle if they are calling in question exonerating the Insurance Companies are hereby dismissed.

32. As stated above, if additional/extra premium is paid covering risk either to owner-driver of the car/jeep or covering risk of pillion rider, then the proof of payment of additional/extra premium is a pure question of fact based on the insurance policies.
Therefore, the insurance policies in each case is to be considered to find out whether additional/extra premium is paid or not.
33...................In these appeals the appellants is/are claimants who are occupants of the private vehicles and hence they are not third party/parties.

Therefore, fastening liability on the appellants/insurance companies are erroneous, hence, appeals are liable to be allowed and the Insurance Company is exonerated for payment of compensation by putting burden to pay compensation on the respondents- owner.
Hence, the appeals are allowed.
In these present appeals the claimants are occupants in the private vehicle and hence they are not third parties.
Therefore, fastening liability on the owner of the private vehicle is correct.
Thus, the Insurance Company is rightly exonerated from the liability to pay compensation.
Therefore, the appeals filed by the claimants and owners are liable to be dismissed.
Accordingly, dismissed.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The respondent No.2 has not lead any evidence to prove their defence that the rider of the bike was not negligent but on materials on record clearly shows that the rider did misjudgment which lead to accident no matter whether it was to avoid a major collision between the car and the bike 13.
The Ex.P.7 which is the copy of charge sheet filed in Cr.No.101/2019 clearly discloses that the investigation officer has filed Sri.Naveen Kumar M vs Sri.H.G.Srinivas Gowda on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14108808/
4 chargesheet after detail investigation holding that the rider of the offending vehicle had ridden it in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and caused the accident.
But under the 'Comprehensive Policy/Package Policy/
liability only policy', the risk of occupants of the car/jeep or pillion on motorcycle are covered as the insured(owner) has entered into contract of insurance with the Insurer for covering risk at higher degree by making payment of extra premium above the horizon of covering risk under the 'Statutory Policy'.
Covering risk of third party is mandatorly made by the statute.
Unless a vehicle is made insured compulsorily so far as covering risk of third party, that vehicle shall not be used on the public places or even in private premises for plying.
Therefore every insured shall purchase insurance policy compulsorily covering risk of third parties before making use the said vehicle for plying either in public place or in private place.
Whereas, if the owner intends to cover higher degree of risk above the covering risk of third parties so as to include covering risk of occupants in the car/jeep or pillion rider on the motorcycle or damaged caused to the vehicle the owner has to pay higher amount of premium covering the risk comprehensively.
Therefore, above the degree of covering the risk of third parties, if the owner intends to cover risk on higher degree as above stated it is because of on own volition of insurer and insured.
Therefore, the degree of covering risk of covering third party only or covering higher degree of risk that depends upon payment of extra premium.
Therefore if extra premium is paid on the own volition of the insured (owner) then it covers higher degree of risk, otherwise not.
Insured (owner) is first party and insurer is second party.
Therefore, the persons who are outside the offending vehicle or may be passengers in another vehicle if it meets with accident by offending vehicle are only terms as third parties considering the definitions enshrined in Section 2(33)
of and Section 2(35) of the M.V.Act with reference to the types of passengers in the said nature of vehicles.
Section 147 of the M.V.Act does not require a policy to cover the risk to passengers who are not carried for hire or reward.
The statutory insurance as mandated in Section 147 of the M.V.Act does not cover injuries suffered by the occupants of the private vehicle or death of the occupants is caused in the accident whether they are carried for hire or reward or not then they are not to be categorized Sri.Naveen Kumar M vs Sri.H.G.Srinivas Gowda on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14108808/
9 as third parties and as such the insurer cannot be held liable under Section 147 of the M.V.Act.
Therefore, considering the definitions enshrined in Section 2(33) and Section 2(35) and Section 147 of the M.V.Act and if they are read harmoniously, the occupants/passengers/inmates of a private vehicle do not fall within the definition of category as third parties. Therefore, the legal obligations made as per Section 147 of the M.V.Act is only to the third parties stated above to those persons stated therein and it cannot extend to the occupants of the car/jeep or pillion rider on the motorcycle as they are not carried for hire or reward in a private service vehicle,
hence, they are not third parties.
26. In public service vehicle the carriage of passengers is on hire or reward basis and for that terms of contract of insurance is different.
But, in private service vehicle the passengers are not carried for hire or reward basis, simply they are occupants in the private service vehicle.
Even giving private service vehicle on hire or reward basis is not correct as per law.
For private service vehicle, it is compulsory to purchase insurance policy for third parties are concerned, but is an option so far as covering risk of occupants in the private service vehicle is concerned.
Therefore, in private service vehicle for covering risk of occupants an additional premium is to be paid.
Therefore, Section 147 of the M.V.Act only covers the risk of third party and to cover the risk in respect of the persons stated therein, but, certainly does not extend covering risk of occupants of the car/jeep or pillion rider on the motorcycle.
27. As discussed above, if insured (owner) intends to cover higher degree of risk than what is covering risk of third parties, then, the insured (owner) shall pay additional premium and it is on volition of insurer and insured as it is pure contract between them in this regard.
In absence of payment of additional premium covering risk of the persons at higher degree apart from third parties, then the insurance companies are not liable to pay compensation.
Therefore, under Section 147 of the M.V.Act the liability arising out of statutory requirement stated therein.
It prescribes compulsorily coverage of risk to third parties and to those who are stated in the said provision.
Therefore, unless the purchase of insurance policy compulsorily at minimal covering the risk of third parties, the owner cannot ply the vehicles on road or on public places and also in private places.
Therefore, the provisions of the M.V.Act are benevolent in nature protecting right and interest of victims arising out of accident particularly who are third parties.
Therefore, for covering risk for occupant in the car/jeep or pillion rider on the motorcycle, then the owner has to pay additional premium.
Therefore, where compulsorily purchase of insurance policy covering third parties only the insurance policy is 'Act'
Policy/Statutory Policy/liability only policy' but under this 'Act Policy/Statutory Policy/ liability only policy' the risk of occupant of the car/jeep or pillion rider is not covered as they are not be categorized as third parties.
